title: How Long Should You Meditate?
excerpt: Most beginners do well with five to ten minutes. Longer is not more virtuous, and research programs use many different lengths.

quick_answer.question: How long should you meditate?
quick_answer.answer: Start with about five to ten minutes. Add time only if you can repeat the session most days. There is no single correct length in tradition or in research.

intro: People want a number so they can know they have done it correctly. The useful number is the one you will repeat, not the longest number you have heard.

sections.heading: What length works for a beginner?
sections.content:
Five to ten minutes is enough to learn a cue such as the breath. Twenty minutes is reasonable later if the short version is already easy to start. An hour is a specialized choice, not a moral minimum. Pain or dread is a reason to shorten, not to endure.

The neighboring page is [daily practice](/articles/daily-meditation-practice/). Treat that link as part of the argument, not as decoration.

sections.heading: What do studies actually use?
sections.content:
Monastic schedules and clinical courses use different lengths because they have different aims. A review of meditation programs does not crown one duration. NCCIH describes practices, not a legal minimum.

A wider map lives at the [meditation topic](/topics/meditation/). Dates and school names matter, because a recent American presentation is often described as if it had no date.

sections.heading: When is longer a bad idea?
sections.content:
Use a timer so you are not negotiating with yourself mid-session. If you miss a day, resume at the same length. Do not double it as punishment. The beginner guide is the place for the first week.

If you want a narrower practical or comparative page, use [meditation for beginners](/articles/meditation-for-beginners/). You can understand the description without joining a group or buying a course.

sections.heading: What should a careful reader refuse?
sections.content:
Do not replace sleep with extra sitting. Do not treat a long session as treatment. If longer sits bring panic, go back to a few minutes or stop and get help.

Readers in the United States often meet a simpler version of the same idea in a class, an app, or a short video. Name that simpler version instead of pretending it is the whole tradition. Traditional teaching, personal report, and research stay in separate sentences on this site. The [editorial policy](/editorial-policy/) is the rule. The [disclaimer](/disclaimer/) applies whenever a sentence leans toward health, safety, or a promised transformation. The [corrections](/corrections/) page is how to challenge a factual mistake. Name the school, the text, or the century whenever a sentence would otherwise float free of history. A reader may stop at the definition when that is all the question required.

key_takeaways: Five to ten minutes is a real start.
Studies do not set one holy duration.
Distress is a reason to shorten.

faq.question: Do traditions demand an hour?
faq.answer: Some intensive settings use long periods. They are not the definition of meditation for a person building a first habit.

faq.question: Is this a full guide?
faq.answer: No. It answers one question and points to the longer page. It is not personal advice.
